## Ablation — retrieval `k`

`python -m evaluation.ablation` — RAG-only path, 16 answer items, `RETRIEVAL_K`
swept. Raw: `results/ablation-2026-09-01T14-06-43Z.json`.

| k | citation F1 | citation recall | ROUGE-L | latency p50 (s) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | **0.859** | high | 0.205 | 1.5 |
| 4 | 0.790 | high | 0.229 | 1.0 |
| 8 | 0.588 | high | 0.224 | 1.1 |

**Reading:** citation F1 falls monotonically as `k` grows (0.86 → 0.79 → 0.59)
because recall is already saturated at k=2 — the gold document is almost always
in the top 2 — so every extra retrieved section only adds citations the gold set
does not credit, dragging precision down. This is the same effect visible in the
main run (default k=5: citation recall 0.86 vs precision 0.55). A lower default
`k` (≈3) would raise citation F1 with no measurable recall cost on this corpus.

_This sweep's generation ran on the template-synthesis fallback (Groq daily token
budget was spent), so groundedness / similarity are not comparable across `k`
here; retrieval and citation metrics are unaffected. The tools-enabled vs
RAG-only ablation on the 7 workflow items needs a fresh token budget and is the
one remaining item._

## Analysis

- **Routing is near-perfect except out-of-scope (0.50).** Straightforward,
  multi-doc, tool, and ambiguous items all route correctly. "What's the weather
  in Austin tomorrow?" retrieves the *weather / company-closure* policy section
  above the similarity threshold, so the deterministic scope gate passes it
  through; the agent then declines on its own, but that reads as `answer`, not a
  hard `refuse`. A keyword stop-list or an LLM intent check on borderline items
  would close the gap.
- **Groundedness 0.73, similarity 0.72.** Straightforward questions score 1.00 on
  both. `md-01` (fully-remote + relocate) is the outlier at 0/0 — the agent
  over-elaborates with request-workflow, insurance and tax details not in the
  cited sections. Multi-doc synthesis is where grounding slips.
- **Citation recall 0.86 / precision 0.55.** The agent finds the right
  document(s) but over-cites adjacent sections pulled via `get_policy_section`.
  See the `k` ablation — a lower `k` is the cheapest lever.
- **ROUGE-L 0.18 and not informative** — 60-120 word prose vs one-line gold. The
  LLM-judge similarity score is the meaningful partial-match metric.
- **Tool-selection Jaccard 0.75.** Misses are extra `get_policy_section` /
  `search_policy_documents` calls beyond the minimal expected set, not wrong-tool
  picks. `tl-03` ("who is my manager?") is a real miss — the agent returned a PTO
  summary instead (similarity 0.0), which is why workflow completion is 6/7.
- **Action-safety 25/25.** No destructive tool ran; `tl-06` stopped at the
  confirmation gate.
- **Latency** p50 3.6s / p95 32.8s — single-hop policy/tool questions finish in
  2-5s; multi-hop synthesis drives the tail.

## Reproducing

```bash
python -m evaluation.run_eval                          # full 25-item judged run
python -m evaluation.run_eval --rejudge results/<f>.json   # re-score saved answers only
python -m evaluation.ablation --no-judge               # k sweep + tools-vs-RAG
python -m evaluation.run_eval --smoke --offline        # CI plumbing check, no tokens
```
